newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Suharto daughter's firm in $2.45 bln road project.
newsitem.headline: Suharto daughter's firm in $2.45 bln road project.

text.p: Indonesia's PT Citra Lamtoro Gung Persada, a conglomerate controlled by one of President Suharto's daughters, said it will launch a 5.82 trillion rupiah ($2.45 billion) tripple-decker road-rail project in April.

"We will launch this project on April 21. Hopefully, we will also then announce the expected participants," Fariza Y. Irawady, head of corporate public relations of the Citra Group, told Reuters on Wednesday.
He said the project would be a joint-venture between Citra, state-owned toll road operator Jasa Marga and state-owned rail company Perumka.
"The three of us will be the majority but we will also cooperate with some foreign partners," Irawady said, declining to name the foreign participants.
"Some of them have confirmed their involvement in this project. We will finalise the agreement soon," he said.
He added the project would be financed by 75 percent loan and 25 percent equity.
The loans will come 60 percent from local sources and 40 percent from offshore, he added.

Irawady said that the tripple-deck structure would consist of a 23.55 km (14.7 mile) toll-road on the upper deck, a 21.25 km (13.2 mile) railway on the middle deck and a public road on the lower deck, linking south Jakarta and downtown Kota in the north.
Jasa Marga and Citra will jointly operate the toll road which will have 22 off-ramps.
Irawady said railway operator Perumka would use the light rail commuter railway track to link 22 stations.
Construction of the project was expected to start by mid-1997 and it is expected to be operational by 2001, he said.

Citra Lamtoro Gung Persada, controlled by Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hardianti Rukmana, focuses mainly on infrastructure projects. The company has a 4.4 percent stake in the listed toll-road company PT Citra Marga.
